title: Daily Debrief — Wednesday Nov 4, 2026
html:
The vote flipped the board: travel up, oil and AI down.

Democrats won both the House and the Senate, and the market rallied, but not evenly. Your travel names ran, and the AI and oil names got hit. Full page: Debrief Nov 4

The one thing

SPY gapped out of its box and closed at $766.81. But it touched $775.64 and gave back $9. Sellers are waiting at $774–776. Hold $762, and the pullback is probably over.

The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,688.62, the Dow rose 3.0%, and the Nasdaq rose 1.4%. The VIX fell about 20% to near 17. Oil fell hard (WTI about $89, Brent below $100), so energy fell while airlines and cruise lines rallied. The 10-year yield dipped to about 4.89%. AI infrastructure sold off on data-center fears (DELL −8.8%, MU −7.0%, NVDA −3.2%). Money went to Amazon (+6.1%) and AAPL (+5.3%) instead. Defense fell on budget worries (LMT −6.9%). Qualcomm fell about 6.6% after hours on its report. ADP showed +86K private jobs in October.

SPY levels

  • $781.62: the Oct 6 record high
  • $774–776: the ceiling. Today's high ($775.64), the 78.6% retracement of the Oct drop ($774.93) and the 1.618× 3-point extension ($774.23) all meet here.
  • $766–768: the middle. The 50% retracement ($765.99), the 50-day ($766.45) and the 20-day ($767.57) overlap. Close: $766.81.
  • $762–763: support. The 38.2% retracement ($762.30), today's low ($762.64) and the 0.786× extension ($763.00).
  • $757: the top of the open gap. $752.30: the line we held Tuesday.
  • $744–748: the 23.6% retracement of the Mar 30 → Oct 6 run, plus the Sep 16 low.
  • $722–727: the 200-day ($727.12) and the 38.2% retracement of the big run ($722.21).

How I read it: a close above $776 opens a run at the record. A close below $762 starts filling the gap. Below $752.30, I'd turn defensive.

Your names that matter today

HLT — $376.53 · +3.5% · record close — Ready on retest

  • What happened: Our trigger fired. We needed a close above $364.50, and it closed at $376.53, a record. Cheaper oil helps travel, and money poured into the group.
  • The chart: A clean uptrend, but RSI is 75. RSI (relative strength index) runs 0–100, and above 70 means the stock has run hot. The old highs at $364.50–368.50 should now act as a floor.
  • I'm watching: A pullback into $364.50–368.50 that holds is the entry. A close below $359.41 (the 23.6% level) cancels it.

DAL — $89.24 · +7.2% — Ready on trigger

  • What happened: Oil fell about 8%, and jet fuel is an airline's second-biggest cost. Delta jumped 7.2%.
  • The chart: Uptrend, RSI 67. It stopped just under the October swing high of $91.95. Above that, the 52-week high is $95.18.
  • I'm watching: A daily close above $91.95 is the trigger. A dip to $85–86 that holds is the second way in. A close below $83 cancels it.

RCL — $333.15 · +6.4% — Wait

  • What happened: It never pulled back to our $307–308 zone. It ran straight to $333 instead. We missed this leg, and that's okay.
  • The chart: RSI 73, sitting on its swing high of $334.56. The old high at $324.55 is the new floor to watch.
  • I'm watching: A dip to about $324.55 that holds. A close below $318 (today's low) means wait for lower. The Dec $360 call is about $860 right now, which is over your $800 cap.

NVDA — $200.13 · −3.2% — Calls off

  • What happened: Democrats won in data-center states, and investors fear tighter rules on AI build-outs. NVDA closed below its 200-day average ($204.39), our cancel line for the call.
  • The chart: The trend is now "mixed": price is under the 200-day while the 50-day is still above it. Today's low of $199.68 is the swing low.
  • I'm watching: A close below $199.68 opens about $194. But your own testing shows put setups have only worked on TSLA, so treat that as low-conviction. A close back above $204.39 puts calls back on the table. Earnings are Nov 17.

XOM — $169.27 · −4.6% — Avoid

  • What happened: The oil-shock theme cracked. WTI fell about 8% to near $89, and Brent dropped below $100 for the first time in weeks. Iran's negotiator read the vote as Americans rejecting the war.
  • The chart: It's sitting right on its 50-day ($168.49) with RSI 43. The uptrend still stands, but the reason for owning it is fading.
  • I'm watching: A close below $168 opens $162.40 (the 78.6% level). Don't buy calls into a theme that's breaking. Mines hit four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, so oil headlines can still whipsaw.

Also: DELL $372.36 (near its $366.62 swing low; no dip-buying). MU $795.23. AAPL $349.51, near its $354.50 high. AMZN $266.03. BA $177, nearing the $181–185 put zone. LMT −6.9%. TSLA on its 200-day ($384.76). NOW flat at $108.81. PLTR $171.70. XOM on its 50-day.

Themes

  • Travel & hotels (HLT · RCL · DAL · ABNB): 88/100. The day's big winner. DAL +7.2%, RCL +6.4%, ABNB +5.6%, HLT at a record.
  • Mega-cap consumer & cloud (AAPL · AMZN · GOOGL): 66/100. AMZN +6.1%, AAPL +5.3%, GOOGL +3.2%. Money went back to the giants.
  • Defensive rotation (KO): 64/100. KO +1.1%, near its high. Quiet and steady.
  • Rates & the Fed (TLT · IWM): 50/100. The 10-year yield eased to about 4.89%. Small caps +1.5%. Friday's jobs report decides it.
  • Defense (LMT · BA): 34/100. LMT −6.9%. A Democratic Congress may trim the $1.5T budget request.
  • Musk complex (TSLA · SPCX): 30/100. TSLA −3.3%, SPCX −3.8%, after Musk spent heavily backing Republicans.
  • Oil shock / Iran (XOM · XLE · USO): 28/100. Flipped. USO −8.1%, XLE −4.7%. The fuel relief now helps travel.
  • AI infrastructure (NVDA · MU · AMD · SMH · DELL · SMCI · BE): 22/100. DELL −8.8%, MU −7.0%, BE −6.4%, NVDA below its 200-day. Data-center scrutiny is the new fear.
  • AI vs software (NOW · PLTR): 18/100. NOW flat, PLTR −2.1%. Still losing.

Lesson of the day: the trigger is your seatbelt, and it cuts both ways

A trigger is the exact price event you decide on before entering. You buy the confirmation, not the idea.

  • The NVDA Dec $220 call wasn't taken because its trigger (a close above $210.94) never fired. It went from $7.44 to $5.15 (−31%), so we avoided about a $230 loss.
  • The RCL Dec $340 call was missed because our dip to $307–308 never came. It went from $8.00 to $16.25 (+103%).

A missed winner costs $0. A forced entry costs real money. Don't chase RCL just because it left without you. See Options Playbook.

Plays on deck

  • HLT Dec 18 $390 call (≈ $775 now · ≈ $475 on the retest · Δ 0.39): Why: the strongest trend on your list, and our trigger fired. Enter: on a pullback to $364.50–368.50 that holds. At about $368, this contract should cost about $475 (estimate, verify in Webull). Exit: a close below $359.41. Targets are $386, then $395. The spread is wide ($7.00–8.50), so use a limit order near the middle.
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 call (≈ $498 · most you can lose · Δ 0.52): Why: cheaper oil means cheaper jet fuel, in an uptrend. Enter: a daily close above $91.95, or a dip to $85–86 that holds. Exit: a close below $83. The target is the $95.18 high. This is a live Webull mid (bid $4.70, ask $5.25).
  • RCL Dec 18 $360 call (≈ $590 on the dip (estimate) · ≈ $860 now · Δ 0.25): Why: the same fuel relief, plus a beat-and-raise quarter. Enter: only on a dip to about $324.55 that holds. Today it's over your $800 cap. Exit: a close below $318. The target is the $350.59 52-week high.

Skip: chasing travel at the open after a gap; XOM or oil calls; NVDA calls (cancelled); ABNB through earnings (IV crush); buying the LMT dip; lottery tickets under 0.20 delta (DELL, MU, AMD, SMH).

Homework

  1. Watch SPY at $762–763. A bounce with a long lower wick means buyers are real. A close below it starts to fill the $757–762.60 gap.
  2. Mark $364.50 and $368.50 on HLT's chart, and look for candles turning up there.

Question: RCL ran 8% past your entry zone without you. What would you need to see before buying it now, and why isn't "I don't want to miss more" on that list?

Macro

Democrats won both chambers. The 10-year yield is about 4.89%. Friday's jobs report and the Dec 8–9 FOMC decide the hike odds. See Fed Tracker and Federal Reserve.
